blocks.text: For Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation, a pending request refers to the status of a formal request initiated by a host or guest partner admin to establish a trusted, cross-tenant relationship with a business partner.
Pending requests for partners provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Approve or deny a B2B Federation request.
Provide granular control over shared resources and user access if approved.

blocks.text: Pending requests streamline the Federation workflow by acting as the intermediate step where:

blocks.item: The guest partner admin submits a request with relevant details (such as tenant name and token).
The host partner admin reviews, validates, and either approves or denies the federation request.
The pending status ensures auditability and security during the decision-making process, avoiding unauthorized or incomplete federations.

blocks.text: After an access token is verified as part of the B2B Federation process, the host and guest partner must approve or deny the pending request on the Pending Requests page. After pending requests are approved, they appear on the Federated Partners page.
On the Pending Requests page (Private Access > B2B Federation > Federation > Pending Requests), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click the Filter icon to display or hide the filters.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. Click Clear to clear the applied filters. To learn more, see Using Tables.
View a list of all pending requests. For each pending request, you can see:
Request Date: The date that the B2B Federation was requested.
Partner: The name of the B2B partner.
Notes: Any additional notes for communication between the B2B partners.
Status: The status of the pending request (i.e., Token Verified, Pending Approval, Pending Verification).
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Update the notes of the pending request.
Approve or deny a pending request.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the Federated Partners page to manage federated partners.
